h: Zeal That Awakens Teshuvah and Wins an Enduring Covenant

p: פִּנְחָס בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר וְגוֹ׳ (בְּמִדְבַּר כה, יא)
הֵשִׁיב אֶת חֲמָתִי מֵעַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳
turned back My wrath from upon the Children of Yisrael, etc.
וְהָיְתָה לּוֹ וּלְזַרְעוֹ אַחֲרָיו וְגוֹ׳ (שָׁם יג)
And it shall be for him and his descendants after him, etc. (ibid. 13),
because he was zealous for his God
and atoned for the Children of Yisrael."
At first glance there is redundancy here
for "because he was zealous for his God"
"in his being zealous with My zeal";
and "and atoned for the Children of Yisrael"
הֵשִׁיב אֶת חֲמָתִי מֵעַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
"turned back My wrath from upon the Children of Yisrael."
At any rate, it should have said:
and atoned for the Children of Yisrael,
in his being zealous with My zeal;
and it shall be for him and his descendants
וְלֹא כִלִּיתִי אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּקִנְאָתִי
"and I did not destroy the Children of Yisrael in My zeal"
is included in what is said,
הֵשִׁיב אֶת חֲמָתִי מֵעַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
"turned back My wrath from upon the Children of Yisrael."
It also needs to be understood
what is meant by "in their midst,"
שֶׁעַל כָּל פָּנִים הָיָה לִכְתּוֹב בָּהֶם
for at any rate it should have written "against them."
And the Ramban, of blessed memory, wrote
that regarding Pinchas it does not say
and it says "My covenant of peace,"
that He gave him covenant with peace;
and of Aharon it is said
and therefore it says "because he was zealous for his God,"
And who is wise that he may know them?
that "for his God" is the lower judgment,
while of Aharon it is written "and for glory,"
and here he explains it as Malchus.
that Malchus too is called peace,
but did not explain his source.
"in his being zealous with My zeal in their midst":
that Pinchas brought thoughts of teshuvah
into the heart of the entire tribe of Shimon
and into the heart of all Yisrael,
for not having protested against them.
who was zealous with the zeal of Hashem,
thoughts of teshuvah were brought into their heart
And this is what is said:
וְלֹא כִלִּיתִי אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּקִנְאָתִי
"and I did not destroy the Children of Yisrael in My zeal":
that even the twenty-four thousand who died,
at any rate their death was an atonement,
like those executed by the beis din,
for all who are executed confess,
has a portion in the World to Come,
they would have been destroyed, Heaven forbid, in their sin
שֶׁהִנְנִי נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶת בְּרִיתִי שָׁלוֹם
"Behold, I give him My covenant of peace":
as is written in the holy Zohar;
"peace" is the attribute of Yosef HaTzaddik,
into the heart of the whole tribe of Shimon and Yisrael
"And it shall be for him and his descendants after him
because he was zealous for his God":
"the law of the kingdom is law"
and that is why he merited the covenant,
the yud of the Name Adnus,
which is the letters of "dina" reversed;
"and atoned for the Children of Yisrael,"
because he brought thoughts of teshuvah into their heart.
And this is the power of Aharon,
who was also one who atones,
שֶׁכִּיפֵּר עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים
who atoned for the Children of Yisrael on Yom HaKippurim,
"For on this day He shall atone, etc.";
but this is the power of Aharon:
through his service on Yom HaKippurim,
and this is what is said,
"For on this day He shall atone, etc."
And so regarding Pinchas it is said,
"and atoned for the Children of Yisrael":
that is, he brought teshuvah into their heart;
and for this he merited for his descendants
But of him it is said
while of Aharon it is written "and for glory,"
which is the aspect of the Holy One, blessed is He,
and Pinchas "was zealous for his God,"
whose effort on his own part
and the yetzer hara clears out from there,
so Pinchas brought thoughts of teshuvah
as it says, "because he was zealous for his God,"
he brought into their heart the upper teshuvah,
And this is why it says "le'Elohav,"
from the yud with the thorn of the yud
and this is how he merited the attribute of peace,
and for his descendants a covenant of eternal kehunah,
